title: Types
description:
C is what is called a _statically typed language_. This means that once somthing of a type exists, it _cannot change types_.
Wait. What are types anyways?
There are 5 main types you will use in C:
- `int`: This stores a whole number, e.g. `12`
- `float`: This stores a 7 digit decimal number. The number literal _must end in 'f'_. e.g. `123.4f`
- `double`: This stoes a 15 digit decimal number, e.g. `123.456789`
- `char`: This stores a character wrapped in _single quotes_. e.g. `'$'`
- `char*`: This is typically used in C to store a string of text wrapped in _double quotes_. (I'll explain the `*` later). e.g. `"Hello, World!"`.
